meetings.title: Stakeholder expectations and project oversight
meetings.attendees: Five participants recorded by Microsoft Teams
meetings.summary: The group discussed the project expectations and how progress would be monitored. The team was expected to operate like a small start-up: organise its own work, establish and follow its own working methods, remain accountable for delivery, and keep the project on track while receiving guidance and oversight from the tutor.
meetings.outcomes: The team would define its Git and project methodology, plan and monitor sprint work, document decisions and evidence, raise blockers early, and use tutor guidance to check direction without transferring ownership of delivery away from the group.

meetings.title: Sprint 1 Scrum coordination meeting
meetings.summary: The team arranged an internal Microsoft Teams meeting during Sprint 1 to coordinate active work and next steps. The meeting was reported by the team as lasting approximately 15 minutes. Detailed minutes were not retained, so the public documentation does not claim specific discussion points that are not supported by a record.
meetings.outcomes: Evidence is retained as proof that the Scrum-style project methodology was used in practice; detailed outcomes are intentionally not invented.

meetings.title: Client/tutor requirements and documentation meeting
meetings.attendees: Tutor MX team and assigned client/tutor
meetings.summary: The team met with the assigned client/tutor to discuss project requirements and documentation expectations. The retained follow-up chat includes a reference documentation wiki shared as an example.
meetings.outcomes: Use the requirements discussion and reference example to improve the documentation website and keep requirement evidence visible.

meetings.title: Daily Scrum / progress checkpoint
meetings.summary: The team discussed current blockers and what information/evidence should be included in the documentation website. The Teams record shows the meeting took place and lasted approximately 26 minutes.
meetings.outcomes: Surface blockers early and strengthen the documentation website with rubric-relevant project evidence.

meetings.title: Sprint workflow retrospective and Sprint 3–4 reorganisation
meetings.summary: Microsoft Teams records the Scrum meeting from 16:58 to 17:17, with a meeting duration of 18m 42s and average attendance of 15m 56s. The team reviewed the Sprint 2 working method and recorded that it was not working well enough for the group.
meetings.outcomes: For Sprint 3 and Sprint 4, work proceeds sequentially Member 1 → Member 2 → Member 3 → Member 4 → Member 5 → Member 6. Each Member starts Branch 1 from the latest main after the previous Member is integrated, creates Branch 2 from their own Branch 1 and Branch 3 from their own Branch 2, and hands over only the cumulative Branch 3 for merging to main.

planning.title: Divide the project into four sprints and six rotating member roles
planning.summary: The planning handbook divides delivery into the four assessed sprints and defines six equal technical roles for each sprint. Before every sprint, the coordinator circulates a poll so each team member can select an available Member 1–6 role. This makes ownership visible, distributes work fairly and allows roles to rotate instead of becoming permanent silos.
planning.outcomes: At the start of each sprint: confirm the sprint goal, run and preserve the role-selection poll, assign one person to each of the six roles, create the role-linked issues and dependencies, and record the final allocation. The handbook is the decision record; dated polls, assigned issues, commits and PRs are the implementation evidence.

planning.title: Select PostgreSQL, Express and Neon instead of Supabase-generated endpoints
planning.summary: The team questioned whether Supabase-generated endpoints would conflict with the brief's requirement to design and implement its own API. After consultation and comparison, the proposed architecture became React + Vite → a team-written Node.js/Express API → Prisma → Neon PostgreSQL. The SQL/Express PDF records why this option provides a clearer handwritten API boundary, front/back separation, demonstrable routes and CI-friendly structure.
planning.outcomes: Use Express for team-owned routes and business logic, Prisma for server-side data access and Neon for PostgreSQL hosting. The browser must never connect directly to Neon. This PDF and discussion prove the decision process; schema, migrations, API commits, integration tests and a deployed database must later prove implementation. The database PDF is AI-assisted, but its original author must confirm the exact tool, model and purpose before submission.

planning.title: Use Gitea main as the source of truth with Member branches and Integration Lead handoff
planning.summary: The current team workflow no longer uses a shared develop branch. Every Member starts from the latest Gitea main, works on a focused issue branch, runs local browser checks and automated tests, pushes the branch, and hands it to the reviewer/Integration Lead. The Integration Lead integrates approved work into main and reruns regression.
planning.outcomes: Gitea main is authoritative. Members do not commit normal feature work directly to main. Before handoff they follow the handbook pages for npm run check, coverage, local browser verification and honest lecturer-runner evidence. Approved Gitea main is synced deliberately to the separate GitHub deployment mirror.

planning.title: Standardise npm run check, local browser verification and honest runner evidence
planning.summary: The current repository full local gate is npm run check. It performs Prisma generation, linting, backend type-checking, backend and frontend tests, production builds and the repository security check. Members also run the affected flow locally before handoff and generate coverage.
planning.outcomes: Local testing is mandatory regardless of remote runner state. If the lecturer-managed Gitea Actions runner is queued/offline, record it as an external blocker and attach local evidence; never claim that specific runner is green when it did not run. Codecov displays coverage generated by tests; it does not run the tests. A separate GitHub deployment-mirror CI/Codecov snapshot was later verified on 25 August 2026.

planning.title: Verify GitHub deployment-mirror CI and create the first dated Codecov snapshot
planning.summary: The tutor-mx-deployment GitHub mirror was made visible to Codecov and its existing CI workflow was rerun. Backend quality/coverage, frontend quality/coverage and the clean PostgreSQL migration/API smoke job all passed. The backend and frontend Codecov upload steps completed using codecov/codecov-action@v5 with OIDC authentication.
planning.outcomes: Retain the 25 August Sprint 1 coverage screenshots as a dated baseline. Codecov shows frontend/src at 81.58% and backend src at 86.37%; the displayed roots contain 2,050 tracked lines, of which 1,715 are covered. Later sprints should append new dated screenshots and percentages instead of replacing this Sprint 1 evidence. This GitHub mirror CI is supplementary release evidence and does not change Gitea main as the official source of truth or imply that the lecturer-managed Gitea runner executed.

planning.title: Apply the course AI policy to planning documents and code
planning.summary: The team adopted the course rule that AI use is allowed only with transparent attribution and human accountability. The handbook declares that this revision was generated and reviewed with Codex[GPT-5]. Every submitted document must declare use or non-use, while AI-generated code commits require an Assisted-by footer.
planning.outcomes: Keep the tool, model and purpose declaration with each AI-assisted document; verify every claim, command and code fragment; remove secrets and personal data before prompting; and keep repository declarations current. For the SQL/Express PDF, confirm and add the exact tool/model/purpose before assessment because its file metadata does not identify them.

planning.title: Plan two team meetings per week
planning.summary: The team discussed a regular cadence consisting of a client-input meeting and an internal progress check. Members proposed meeting twice a week, with once a week as the minimum when availability is limited.
planning.outcomes: Aim for two meetings each week: one stakeholder/client touchpoint where available and one internal tracking meeting. Record attendance, decisions, actions and proof in the Meeting Record section after each meeting.

planning.title: Adopt automatic Auth0 role/Profile onboarding and direct saved-role routing
planning.summary: New users choose Student, Tutor or Organiser before Auth0. After authentication, React calls POST /api/auth/onboarding and the Express backend verifies identity and creates/links the matching Neon Profile through Prisma. Existing linked users use /api/me and go directly to their saved workspace without a second role choice.
planning.outcomes: Normal sign-up no longer requires manually creating Neon Profile rows or assigning individual Tutor Mx roles by hand. Use separate test accounts for different roles. Email verification remains part of Auth0 identity handling.

planning.title: Use registered Tutor accounts in Organiser Tutor Management
planning.summary: Tutor accounts appear after tutors use the normal self-service Tutor sign-up flow. Organisers search by name/email and edit the database-backed Tutor record. Technical Auth0 subject/User ID fields were removed from the normal organiser interface.
planning.outcomes: Later sprints harden and extend this registered-Tutor flow. They must not reintroduce a manual Auth0-subject tutor-create form.

planning.title: Adopt sequential Member handoffs and cumulative branch chains for Sprint 3–4
planning.summary: The Sprint 2 organisation created excessive coordination and merge overhead. The team agreed not to repeat it for the remaining sprints.
planning.outcomes: Members work strictly in order 1 through 6. Within each Member, task Branch 2 is created from Branch 1 and task Branch 3 from Branch 2. Branch 3 is cumulative and is the only branch merged to main. The next Member begins only after that merge and regression check.
